parole.testo: From -uș + -ior, from Albanian -sh + Latin -olus.

Unknown. Possibly a substratum word, perhaps from a Dacian *bengas, *bongas or *bungas, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂ǵnos, with a suffix added later, akin to Albanian bung. Alternatively, a borrowing from this Albanian word.
Unknown. Possibly a substratum word, akin to Albanian burdhë (“bag, sack”). Alternatively, a borrowing from this Albanian word. Cognate of Russian бурдюк (burdjuk).
Probably borrowed from Albanian qafë, of uncertain origin. May be cognate to Ancient Greek κεφαλή (kephalḗ, “head”). Unrelated to Turkish kafa (“head”).

From older copaci (compare Aromanian cupaci, Megleno-Romanian cupaci, Istro-Romanian copaț (“thicket, brushwood”)), possibly borrowed from Albanian kopaç (“treestump”) or cognate to it as a Balkan substrate root. The current form was probably analogically formed as a singular from the earlier copaci
Probably from Albanian kurpen, kurpën, variant of kulpër.

Substratum word, akin to Albanian kurth, kurthë, or possibly borrowed from it. Alternatively from the feminine of curs, past participle of cure and curge (cf. also Medieval Latin cursa (“incursion”)).
Substratum word, akin to or derived from Albanian këpushë, or from a diminutive of cap + -ușă. Also cognate to Aromanian cãpush(ã), dialectal Bulgarian капуш (kapuš).

Substratum word, akin to Albanian katund (northern/Gheg variant katûn), or possibly derived from it. Probably of native Balkanic, possibly Illyrian origin, and ultimately Indo-European but it is a much-disputed word with numerous and varied attempted etymologies. It is also found in many Balkan Slav

It is uncertain whether the noun fluture came before it or was derived from it. Probably ultimately of imitative origin, through a hypothetical *fâltura. Or linked to Albanian and possibly derived from it; compare flutur. Cognate with Aromanian flitur, fliturari. Other theories suggest a Vulgar Lati

Unknown. Possibly from a root *flutulus, or deverbative from flutura. Related to Albanian flutur, and possibly derived from it; alternatively, it may have a substratum root akin to it, or simply be of imitative origin. Compare also Aromanian flitur.
Aphetic form of sfărâmă, possibly from Albanian thërrime, or a substratum term cognate to it. Alternatively from the verb fărâma.
Akin to Aromanian guvã (“hole, cavity”), likely ultimately from Albanian guvë (“pit, cave”).

Unknown. Moș and its feminine counterpart moașă (“midwife; old woman”) (which appears to be older) are often considered substratum words related to Albanian moshë or derived from it, but can also possibly be from Latin annōsus (“aged, old, full of years”) with a loss of the initial vowel as in some

Probably a substratum word, akin to or derived from Albanian mugull. Also, possibly from a Vulgar Latin root *muculus, diminutive of Latin mūcus, or simply reformed as a singular from mucuri as the plural of muc.

Origin disputed. * Compare Aromanian mãndzu, Megleno-Romanian mǫndz; possibly from or related and cognate to Albanian (Gheg) mâz (compare standard mëz and Old Albanian manz) through the substratum, or of Illyrian origin. * Compare the Thracian word mezenai (“horse”) and Messapic Menzana, a horse dei

Possibly a substratum word, akin to or borrowed from Albanian magar. A less likely theory derives it from Latin onāgrārius (from onager) through a Vulgar Latin root *onagarius, which resulted in a hypothetical *unăgariu in early Romanian, leading to un *năgar and ultimately its current state (compar
Probably derived from Albanian ujanë or from naie (“ship”) + -an. Possibly a substrate word from Thraco-Dacian.

Possibly borrowed from Albanian nepërkë (“adder, viper”), otherwise cognate to it, from fuller nepërtkë, originally ‘hatchling snake’, maybe from Proto-Slavic *nepъrtъkъ (compare Bulgarian непрътък (neprătăk, “buttercup”)). Compare Aromanian nipãrticã.

Compare Megleno-Romanian pupează. Most likely an imitative substratum word, akin to Albanian pupëzë, or possibly derived from a root pupă (now found only in Aromanian), of onomatopoetic origin, with suffix -ză. Other languages show similar forms, compare Latin upupa, Sardinian pubùsa, pupùsa, French

Might be a deverbal from Albanian shqipe, shkype, modern forms of the old term Albanian shkabë (“eagle”); which derived from Proto-Albanian *iš-gabā, from Proto-Indo-European *kobuǵos. A cognate to English hawk, Latin capys (“bird of prey”) and Russian ко́бец (kóbec, “falcon”).
Borrowed from Albanian shqipëtar.

Unknown. Possibly from archaic scrumb; a substratum word, akin to or from Albanian shkrumb. Other theories include Cuman Turkic kurum ("soot") (cf. Hungarian korom). Alternatively, it may simply be from an expressive root.
Borrowed from Albanian shpuzë, from Latin spodium.
Probably from Albanian trastë

parole.significato: a type of unripened whey cheese, similar to ricotta.
parole.testo: Unknown. Possibly a Dacian substratum word, akin to Albanian urdhë, or more likely derived/borrowed from it. Unknown. Possibly from Albanian vapë (“hot weather”), from Old Italian vapa (“vapor”), from Latin vapor (“heat, hot air”), though the relationship between the words is uncertain. Another theory is that it is linked to a Vulgar Latin root *vapalia, from vapa. Compare Sicilian vampa.

parole.significato: buttermilk (liquid left over after producing butter)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Albanian dhallë.
Borrowed from Albanian shpagë (“compensation, payment to end a blood feud”), from Italian paga (“payment”).
Possibly borrowed from Albanian thep (“peak, point”) or cep (“edge, tip”) or a substratum term cognate to it. Compare also Italian zeppa, inzeppare and Proto-Slavic *cĕpa.
